_format: Two independent AI systems, driven by two independent tables, gated by two independent conditions -- do not conflate them. (A) MOVE CHOICE: engine/battle/trainer_ai.asm's AIEnemyTrainerChooseMoves runs on every single enemy move selection, every turn, no exceptions. It starts a per-move 'weight' buffer at 10 for each of the enemy's 4 move slots (lower = more likely to be picked; ties are chosen at random among the surviving minimum), then walks TrainerClassMoveChoiceModifications (data/trainers/move_choices.asm, INCLUDEd into trainer_ai.asm) for the current wTrainerClass: `ld hl, TrainerClassMoveChoiceModifications / ld a,[wTrainerClass] / ld b,a` then skips (b-1) zero-terminated entries and reads the current entry's layer-id byte list, dispatching each id (1/2/3/4) through AIMoveChoiceModificationFunctionPointers before finally picking the lowest-weighted surviving move(s). This is what 'moveChoiceLayers' below encodes. (B) ITEM USE / SWITCHING: engine/battle/trainer_ai.asm's TrainerAI is called once per turn from engine/battle/core.asm (`callfar TrainerAI`, both in the enemy-moves-first and player-moves-first branches of the turn order code, immediately before the enemy's move would execute). It indexes TrainerAIPointers (data/trainers/ai_pointers.asm) by trainer class: `ld a,[wTrainerClass] / dec a / ... ld hl, TrainerAIPointers / add hl,bc / add hl,bc / add hl,bc` (3 bytes/entry: count, ptr_lo, ptr_hi), lazily initializes the per-Pokemon-use countdown wAICount from the entry's count byte the first time it's called for a newly-sent-out enemy mon (wAICount is reset to the sentinel $FF every time EnemySendOut runs, in engine/battle/core.asm, so each new active enemy Pokemon gets a fresh budget of `count` uses), rolls `call Random`, and jumps into the trainer-class-specific AI subroutine below with that random byte in `a`. If the subroutine performs an action (item use or switch), it calls DecrementAICount (which also sets carry), and engine/battle/core.asm's turn logic (`jr c, .AIActionUsedEnemyFirst`) SKIPS the enemy's actual move entirely that turn -- using an item/switching consumes the whole turn, it is not a free action. This is what 'aiCount'/'aiRoutine'/the itemUse behavior below encodes. GenericAI (`and a / ret`) means a trainer class has NO item-use/switch behavior at all -- move choice modification layers still apply to it independently via table (A).

_notes.layer1: AIMoveChoiceModification1 (data/trainers/move_choices.asm layer id 1): discourages non-damaging status moves when the player's active mon is already statused. Code: `ld a,[wBattleMonStatus] / and a / ret z` -- bails immediately (no effect) if the player's mon has no status ailment at all. Otherwise, for each of the enemy's 4 moves it reads the move's power and effect; if power==0 AND the move's effect is in StatusAilmentMoveEffects (EFFECT_01 [unused sleep effect], SLEEP_EFFECT, POISON_EFFECT, PARALYZE_EFFECT), it adds 5 to that move's weight buffer entry (`add $5`) -- since lower weight wins, this heavily discourages (but does not fully forbid) re-inflicting a redundant status.
_notes.layer2: AIMoveChoiceModification2 (layer id 2): slightly encourages certain non-damaging support-move effect ranges. Gated globally by `ld a,[wAILayer2Encouragement] / cp $1 / ret nz` -- it ONLY has any effect when wAILayer2Encouragement equals exactly 1. wAILayer2Encouragement is reset to 0 every time a new enemy Pokemon is sent out (engine/battle/core.asm, EnemySendOut: `ld [wAILayer2Encouragement], a` with a=0) and is incremented by 1 every time an enemy move is actually executed (engine/battle/core.asm, ExecuteEnemyMove: `ld hl, wAILayer2Encouragement / inc [hl]`) -- so this layer is active for exactly one move selection per enemy Pokemon's battle lifetime: the SECOND move it ever chooses (right after its first move has executed), never before and never again after. When active, for each move it checks the move's effect id against two hardcoded ranges -- [ATTACK_UP1_EFFECT, BIDE_EFFECT) and [ATTACK_UP2_EFFECT, POISON_EFFECT) -- and if the effect falls in either range, decrements that move's weight by 1 (slight encouragement); everything else is untouched. This is a narrow, easily-mis-ported quirk: a naive port that applies layer 2 'whenever an effect is stat-boosting' every turn would over-trigger it relative to the original.
_notes.layer3: AIMoveChoiceModification3 (layer id 3): type-effectiveness-based encourage/discourage. For each of the enemy's 4 moves it calls `AIGetTypeEffectiveness` against the player's current mon. If effectiveness == $10 (neutral/1x), no change. If > $10 (super effective), decrement that move's weight by 1 (encourage). If < $10 (not very effective / immune), it does NOT unconditionally discourage -- it first scans the enemy's WHOLE moveset for a 'better move' (Super Fang, any SPECIAL_DAMAGE_EFFECT move [e.g. Dragon Rage/Sonic Boom], Fly, or any other damaging move of a different type than the weak move being evaluated); only if such a better alternative exists does it increment (discourage) the weak move's weight by 1. Net effect matches the task description: prefer super-effective moves, avoid resistant/ineffective damaging moves ONLY when something better is available, otherwise leave them alone (better to hit for reduced damage than not attack at all).
_notes.layer4: AIMoveChoiceModification4 exists as a 4th function-pointer slot but is a no-op (`ret`) and is never referenced by any entry in TrainerClassMoveChoiceModifications -- confirmed unused, not included in the id lists above.
_notes.moveChoiceMechanism: AIEnemyTrainerChooseMoves seeds all 4 weight slots to 10, force-sets any currently-Disabled move's slot to 50 (near-certain exclusion) before running the layers, then after all layers run, finds the minimum surviving weight value and zeroes out (disables) every move slot that isn't tied for that minimum, returning the filtered array for random selection among the (usually single) remaining move(s).

_itemUse._mechanism: Each per-class AI subroutine (engine/battle/trainer_ai.asm) receives a fresh `call Random` byte in `a` from TrainerAI before it runs. Most gate on `cp N percent + 1 / ret nc` (proceed only if the random roll is below a threshold ~= N% of 256, since the `percent` macro is `* $ff / 100`, macros/data.asm) and/or `AICheckIfHPBelowFraction` (proceed only if the active enemy mon's current HP is below 1/N of its max). Any action taken consumes one of the class's per-Pokemon aiCount uses via DecrementAICount, and replaces the enemy's move for that turn entirely (see _format).

byClass.BLACKBELT: ~13% chance per turn to use X Attack (AIUseXAttack) -- raises Attack, no HP gate.
byClass.GIOVANNI: ~25% chance per turn to use Guard Spec (AIUseGuardSpec) -- prevents stat drops (Mist), no HP gate.
byClass.COOLTRAINER_M: ~25% chance per turn to use X Attack (AIUseXAttack), no HP gate.
byClass.COOLTRAINER_F: Confirmed vanilla-game BUG: the source has the `ret nc` for its intended ~25% switch-chance check commented out (`; ret nc`, with the comment 'The intended 25% chance to consider switching will not apply.'), so the percent roll is computed but never actually gates anything -- the routine ALWAYS runs every turn: if HP < 1/10 max, use Hyper Potion (AIUseHyperPotion, heals 200); else if HP < 1/5 max, switch out if 2+ healthy mons remain (AISwitchIfEnoughMons); otherwise do nothing. Port this bug faithfully unless asked to fix it.
byClass.BROCK: Unconditional (no percent roll, no HP gate): if his active mon currently has ANY status condition, use Full Heal (AIUseFullHeal) to cure it.
byClass.MISTY: ~25% chance per turn to use X Defend (AIUseXDefend), no HP gate.
byClass.LT_SURGE: ~25% chance per turn to use X Speed (AIUseXSpeed), no HP gate.
byClass.ERIKA: ~50% chance per turn AND HP < 1/10 max -> use Super Potion (AIUseSuperPotion, heals 50).
byClass.KOGA: ~25% chance per turn to use X Attack (AIUseXAttack), no HP gate.
byClass.BLAINE: ~25% chance per turn to use Super Potion (AIUseSuperPotion, heals 50) -- no HP gate at all, can heal at full HP.
byClass.SABRINA: ~25% chance per turn AND HP < 1/10 max -> use Hyper Potion (AIUseHyperPotion, heals 200).
byClass.RIVAL2: ~12.5% chance per turn ('13 percent - 1') AND HP < 1/5 max -> use Potion (AIUsePotion, heals 20).
byClass.RIVAL3: ~12.5% chance per turn ('13 percent - 1') AND HP < 1/5 max -> use Full Restore (AIUseFullRestore, full heal HP + cures status).
byClass.LORELEI: ~50% chance per turn AND HP < 1/5 max -> use Super Potion (AIUseSuperPotion, heals 50).
byClass.BRUNO: ~25% chance per turn to use X Defend (AIUseXDefend), no HP gate.
byClass.AGATHA: Two independent checks: if roll < ~8%, switch out if 2+ healthy mons remain (AISwitchIfEnoughMons, no HP gate); else if roll < ~50% AND HP < 1/4 max, use Super Potion (AIUseSuperPotion).
byClass.LANCE: ~50% chance per turn AND HP < 1/5 max -> use Hyper Potion (AIUseHyperPotion, heals 200).
byClass.JUGGLER: ~25% chance per turn to switch out if 2+ healthy mons remain (AISwitchIfEnoughMons); not an item, a mon swap. Shared by JUGGLER and UNUSED_JUGGLER (both point at JugglerAI).
byClass.GenericAI (all classes not listed above): No item use, no switching, no special behavior at all (`and a / ret`) -- these classes only ever use move-choice layers to pick among their existing moves.
